issues.title: Publish or classify the 377 DRAFT Shopify products blocking checkout
issues.description:
## Problem
398 of 2,330 SKUs (17%) cannot be purchased. 377 sit on Shopify products in DRAFT + unpublished state; Shopify answers their cart permalink with **HTTP 410 Gone**.

## Evidence
```
DRAFT   GB-RND-FRS-78ML-RDC-MSLV  → /cart/53343606112548:1  → HTTP 410 Gone
ACTIVE  (control)                 → /cart/53343616598308:2  → HTTP 302 → real checkout
```
Spread across 13 families: Elegant 77 · Round 48 · Diva 43 · Sleek 36 · Slim 36 · Circle 34 · Cylinder 24 · Empire 24 · Sprayer 15 · Atomizer 12 · Grace 12 · Diamond 12 · Lotion Pump 7.

Full list: `data/audits/launch-readiness-2026-07-29/shopify-blocked-skus-prod.json`

## Decision needed from Abbas
Were these held back deliberately (discontinued / not yet launched), or never published?

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Abbas confirms per-family or per-SKU intent
- [ ] Intentionally-available SKUs set to ACTIVE + published to Online Store in Shopify
- [ ] Intentionally-unavailable SKUs documented so they stay quote-only
- [ ] `scripts/sync_shopify_sellability.mjs --apply` re-run
- [ ] `npx convex run products:getCheckoutBlockedCount --prod` returns only the intended count

issues.title: DECISION: volume pricing model — Shopify quantity rules vs quote-only
issues.description:
## Problem
The site displays a volume ladder; Shopify's cart permalink charges the flat 1-piece price. Verified with a real checkout:
```
GB-DVA-CLR-46ML-T-06
  Tier says:        $7.46/ea at 12+  → $89.49 for 12
  Shopify charged:  $7.85/ea (1pc)   → $94.20 for 12
```

## Why this is urgent at our actual order sizes
Average order is 100–1,000 units. Measured against production:

| Order size | SKUs with a better price hidden | Avg overcharge per line |
|---|---|---|
| 100 | 5.0% | $13.45 |
| 250 | **98.3%** | $83.96 |
| 500 | **98.3%** | $195.48 |
| 1,000 | **98.5%** | $412.37 |

On legacy bestbottles.com the same 500-unit order bills at the 144/210 tier. On the new site it bills at 1pc. **We are migrating customers to a site that charges ~15% more for the same order.**

## Options
**(a)** Configure Shopify quantity rules (we are on Shopify **Plus**, so this is included), then flip `NEXT_PUBLIC_VOLUME_TIERS_HONORED_AT_CHECKOUT=true`.
**(b)** Keep volume strictly quote-only — ship as it currently stands (PDP labels tiers "By Quote").

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Abbas picks (a) or (b) in writing
- [ ] If (a): BB-004 and BB-005 are unblocked
- [ ] If (b): confirm sales will honor ladder prices on quotes, and BB-006 still proceeds

issues.title: Configure Shopify quantity price rules to honor the volume ladder
issues.description:
## Task
Only if BB-003 resolves to option (a). Implement Shopify Plus quantity rules / volume pricing so the checkout total matches the advertised ladder.

Breakpoints are per-product and case-derived: 1 / 12 / 144 / 600 / 3000 plus case multiples (210, 216, 224, 240, 270, 288, …). Source of truth is `products.priceTiers` in Convex (2,305 of 2,330 SKUs, loaded in #57 with an accuracy gate).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A qty-12 checkout on `GB-DVA-CLR-46ML-T-06` totals **$89.49**, not $94.20
- [ ] A qty-500 checkout matches the ladder tier for that SKU
- [ ] `node scripts/audit_price_parity.mjs` shows 0 mismatches at tier quantities
- [ ] `NEXT_PUBLIC_VOLUME_TIERS_HONORED_AT_CHECKOUT=true` set in Vercel production
- [ ] Cart subtotal equals Shopify checkout total end-to-end

issues.title: Surface the full price ladder on the PDP (144 / 600 / 3000 tiers)
issues.description:
## Problem
The PDP renders only the 1 / 10 / 12 slice from `webPrice1pc/10pc/12pc`. The real ladder lives in `products.priceTiers` and runs far deeper.

```
GB-SLM-BLK-5ML-ATM-BLK-T
  1     $2.25      144   $2.03
  12    $2.14      600   $1.91      3000  $1.76
```

At our average order size (100–1,000 units) **98.3% of SKUs have a better price the customer qualifies for and never sees**.

## This is a regression, not a gap
Legacy bestbottles.com shows all five tiers inline **on the category page**, with a live quantity calculator:
```
Pack Of : 1 pcs - $0.39/pc  12 pcs - $4.45($0.37/pc)  144 pcs - $50.54($0.35/pc)
          576 pcs - $190.94($0.33/pc)  2880 pcs - $876.10($0.30/pc)
Qty: [__]  Add to  →  Total Quantity: __   Price: __
```
SKS Bottle (industry leader) does the same. We are the only one hiding it.

## Scope
Render from `priceTiers`, not the legacy 1pc/10pc/12pc trio. Note `webPrice10pc` is vestigial — only 53 SKUs have a real 10-unit break; 2,252 break at 12.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] PDP shows every tier in `priceTiers` with per-unit **and** line total
- [ ] Active tier highlighted for the entered quantity
- [ ] "Add N more to reach $X/ea" nudge to the next break
- [ ] Copy matches whichever BB-003 option was chosen
- [ ] Falls back gracefully for the 25 SKUs with no `priceTiers`

issues.title: DECISION: sell by case or by unit
issues.description:
## Problem
83–86% of typical orders (100–1,000 units) are **partial cases**. Case quantities run 210 / 216 / 224 / 240 / 270 / 288, and the PDP says "order any quantity." The tier breakpoints are themselves case-derived, so the underlying pricing model is case-based while the storefront presents per-unit.

## Industry comparison
- **SKS Bottle**: `221/cs | $238.68 ($1.08 each)` — sells by case, shows per-each in parentheses
- **Calaso**: quantity stepper rounds to "(Safe)Pack", states MOQ and pcs/pallet

## Questions for Abbas
- Does the warehouse actually break cases at 100–1,000 units, or does someone round up by hand after the order lands?
- Should the site enforce case multiples, or keep "any quantity"?
- Is there a real MOQ?

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Decision recorded
- [ ] If case-based: PDP shows case price + per-each, quantity snaps to case multiples, MOQ enforced

issues.title: Push variant weights to Shopify (2,164 available from Convex)
issues.description:
## Problem
**0 of 2,309** Shopify variants carry a weight, and every one is flagged `requiresShipping: true`. Carrier-calculated rates (FedEx/UPS live rates) cannot price a parcel with no weight — the customer sees no shipping option, or a wrong one.

## Good news
Convex already holds `bottleWeightG` for 2,168 products and `caseWeightG` for 2,035 — **2,164 of the 2,309 are fixable by a push**, not by re-measuring.

Data: `data/audits/launch-readiness-2026-07-29/shopify-zero-weight-skus.json`

## Blocked on
BB-013 (shipping model) — if we go flat-rate, weights are lower priority; for live rates they are mandatory.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Write a dry-run-by-default push script following the `sync_shopify_sellability.mjs` pattern
- [ ] Weights written to `inventoryItem.measurement.weight` with correct unit
- [ ] Re-run `scripts/audit_shipping_readiness.mjs` → `variantsWithRealWeight` ≥ 2,164
- [ ] Test checkout returns a real carrier rate

issues.title: DECISION: free-shipping threshold is effectively unconditional at B2B volumes
issues.description:
## Problem
The site promises free shipping over **$99**. At our real order sizes that means free freight on essentially every order:

| Order size | Orders clearing $99 |
|---|---|
| 100 units | 64.9% |
| 250 units | 96.6% |
| 500 units | 99.7% |
| 1,000 units | 100.0% |

Heavy, breakable glass, no weights configured, no carrier answers — this is unbounded freight liability.

## Also: the number contradicts itself
- Site banner + PDP: **$99**
- `convex/knowledge.ts` + `/example` page: **$199**

## Industry comparison
SKS Bottle sets theirs at **$350** (US) / $500 (CA) and sells by case. Calaso quotes freight per order.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Correct threshold confirmed by Abbas
- [ ] Single source of truth in code; all copy updated
- [ ] Threshold actually configured in Shopify, not just written on the site

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Token rotated and updated in Vercel + `.env.local` (coordinate with BB-041)
- [ ] `scripts/audit_shipping_readiness.mjs` extended to report zones and rates

issues.title: Collect box sizes and packing weights
issues.description:

We know bottle weights, but not the parcel:
- What boxes do you ship in? (dimensions)
- Packing material weight per box?
- Do you ship loose units, or only full cases?

Without these, even with variant weights, carrier rates will be wrong — the dimensional weight of glass in a box is what actually prices.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Box catalogue with dimensions + tare weight
- [ ] Packing rules documented
- [ ] Configured in Shopify packages

issues.title: Define the freight/LTL cutover quantity
issues.description:
## Needed from Abbas
At 3,000+ units this becomes pallets and LTL freight, not parcel. At what quantity does an order stop being a normal shipment and need a freight quote?

This matters because the price ladder runs to 15,840 units — the site will happily accept an order it cannot parcel-ship.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Above it, checkout routes to a freight quote instead of a parcel rate

issues.title: Wire form submissions to email/Slack notification
issues.description:
## Problem
`convex/forms.ts` writes every quote, sample, contact, and newsletter submission into `formSubmissions` and **stops there**. No email integration exists anywhere in the codebase (verified: no Resend, SendGrid, Postmark, Nodemailer, or Slack webhook). The only reader is `listByType`, an `internalQuery` no UI can call.

A quote request is invisible unless somebody opens the Convex dashboard.

## Why this is urgent
Quotes are the fallback path for all 398 unsellable SKUs *and* for all volume pricing. It is the primary conversion path right now — and it is unmonitored.

## Needed from Abbas
- Destination email address(es)
- Slack/SMS alerts too?
- Who owns responding, and within what SLA?

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Provider chosen and configured
- [ ] Every `forms.submit` triggers a notification containing all line items
- [ ] Failure to notify is logged, never silent
- [ ] Test submission received end-to-end

issues.title: Build an internal view for form submissions

issues.title: Restore structured RFQ line items (currently dead code)
issues.description:
## Problem
`FormPage.tsx:92` is the only producer of structured quote line items, fed exclusively from `sessionStorage['bb-rfq-line-items']`. The only writer (`persistQuoteDraft` in CartDrawer) was deleted this week, so **every quote now submits an empty `rfqLineItems` array**.

Sales receives free-text `products`/`quantities` blobs instead of resolvable SKUs, variant IDs, quantities, unit prices, and neck sizes.

## Direction
Cart-level quote CTAs are deliberately gone — a cart is for checking out (confirmed with Jordan, and it matches both Calaso and SKS: one cart, one purpose). Calaso still captures a structured line-item list, they just capture it **before** the cart.

So: have the PDP "Request a Quote" button write `bb-rfq-line-items` for that product.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] PDP quote CTA writes the structured draft
- [ ] A quote submitted from a PDP arrives with populated `rfqLineItems`
- [ ] No quote CTA reintroduced in cart or cart drawer
- [ ] If rejected, remove the orphaned reader and the line-item editor UI instead

issues.title: Cut Clerk over to its production instance
issues.description:
## Problem
Vercel **production** runs Clerk's **development** instance. Verified three ways:
```
Backend API  → GET /v1/instance → environment_type: "development"
Vercel prod  → pk_test_… / sk_test_…
frontend     → instanceEnvironmentType: "development"
```
Host: `together-lemur-38.clerk.accounts.dev`. Only domain: `together.lemur-38.lcl.dev`. 4 users.

Consequences: hard user cap (~100), "Development mode" badge visible to customers, dev-grade sessions, instance can be reset.

Note: the dashboard URL Jordan supplied points at `ins_3EyaM8yXPtZB8lTO6AUP7T43Oe2`, a **different** instance in the same app — likely the production one already exists. **Users do not migrate between instances.**

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Production instance confirmed/configured
- [ ] Production domain added, DNS records (clerk., accounts., clkmail.) verified
- [ ] `pk_live_`/`sk_live_` set in Vercel production
- [ ] Paths set: sign-in `/sign-in`, sign-up `/sign-up`, after-auth `/portal`
- [ ] Best Bottles logo uploaded (currently `logoImageUrl: null`)
- [ ] "Development mode" badge gone from the live site

issues.title: Create a Google Cloud OAuth client before Clerk production cutover
issues.description:
## Problem — this is the cutover trap
Google sign-in is enabled and working today (`socialEnabled: ["oauth_google"]`), but a **development** Clerk instance uses Clerk's **shared** Google OAuth app. Production instances reject those.

**Google sign-in will break the moment we flip to `pk_live_`** unless our own Google Cloud OAuth client exists first. It works right up until it doesn't, which is why this gets missed.

## Needed
- A Google Cloud account/project (Abbas or us?)
- OAuth consent screen branded Best Bottles
- Client ID + secret pasted into Clerk → SSO → Google
- Authorized redirect URI from the Clerk dashboard

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Own OAuth client created
- [ ] Consent screen shows "Best Bottles", not accounts.dev
- [ ] Google sign-in verified on the production instance before DNS cutover

issues.title: DECISION: portal onboarding — invite-only or self-serve organizations
issues.description:
## Problem
The B2B portal keys off a Clerk **organization**. With none active it shows "Choose your organization to use the portal." So **a customer who signs up on their own reaches a portal they cannot use** — a dead end.

Current sign-up config: email (required) → verification code → password (required); first/last name **optional**; no phone; no company field.

## Options
- **Invite-only** — Abbas approves each customer. Works today; the `ticket` attribute is already enabled.
- **Self-serve** — anyone signs up and creates/joins an org. Needs Organizations with self-serve creation enabled and a company field at sign-up.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Decision recorded
- [ ] Onboarding path implemented end-to-end with no dead end
- [ ] A brand-new account reaches a functioning portal

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Test orgs (TestCompany, My Organization) removed or renamed
- [ ] Portal dashboard renders terms, credit, and orders for a signed-in org

issues.title: Make first/last name required at sign-up
issues.description:

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Sign-up form no longer shows "Optional" on names
- [ ] Existing 4 users backfilled or prompted

issues.title: Replace the invalid OpenAI key on prod Convex (Grace text mode is down)

```bash
npx convex env set OPENAI_API_KEY sk-... --prod
```

## Important
Grace's *retrieval* layer is healthy — 36/36 matrix, all catalog tools pass, ElevenLabs voice and signed-url OK. **Only the text LLM call is broken.** Voice mode is unaffected.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `node scripts/eval_grace.mjs` returns real scores, not INFRA_ERROR
- [ ] Text Grace answers a catalog question on staging

issues.title: Unknown product URLs return HTTP 200 instead of 404
issues.description:
## Problem
`/products/does-not-exist-xyz` returns **HTTP 200** with a "Product Not Found" body. It is correctly `noindex`, so SEO damage is limited, but Google prefers a real 404 and soft-404s waste crawl budget.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Missing products call `notFound()` and return 404
- [ ] Legacy route overrides still redirect correctly (301, not 404)

issues.title: DECISION: confirm the launch domain and DNS cutover
issues.description:
## Problem
Sitemap and canonicals emit `https://www.bestbottles.com` — which currently serves the **legacy PHP site**. Staging runs at `best-bottles-website.vercel.app`.

Launch means pointing bestbottles.com at the new app. That needs explicit confirmation, because everything else (Clerk domain, Sanity CORS, Shopify, OG tags) keys off it.

## Questions
- Confirmed that bestbottles.com is the launch domain?
- Who controls DNS?
- Target date?

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Domain and date confirmed
- [ ] `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` correct in Vercel production
- [ ] Clerk, Sanity CORS, and Shopify allowed origins updated in lockstep

issues.title: Define returns policy and terms
issues.description:
## Needed from Abbas
- Return window and restocking fee?
- Who pays return shipping?
- Minimum order? Any SKU-level minimums?

SKS publishes "free online returns up to 45 days" as a competitive differentiator; we currently have a `/shipping-returns` page that needs real numbers.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Policy confirmed and published
- [ ] Matches whatever Shopify enforces

issues.title: Verify tax configuration and wholesale exemption handling
issues.description:
## Needed
- Is Shopify tax calculation configured for every state we sell into?
- How are tax-exempt wholesale customers handled at checkout?

The portal already models `taxExempt` on `portalAccounts`, but nothing connects it to Shopify checkout.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Tax registration/nexus confirmed with Abbas
- [ ] Exempt customers verified not charged tax at checkout
- [ ] Path documented for a customer to submit an exemption certificate

issues.title: Enable Shopify test mode for the demo, and disable before launch
issues.description:
## Task
To demo a completed purchase without a real charge, enable test mode in Shopify Payments (Settings → Payments → Manage → test mode). Complete the flow with a test card — real order record, no real money.

**Must be turned OFF before real launch**, or live orders will not capture payment.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Test mode enabled for the demo
- [ ] Full flow demoed: catalog → PDP → cart → checkout → confirmation
- [ ] Test mode disabled and verified before go-live
- [ ] Test orders cancelled/archived

issues.title: Rotate all credentials exposed in git history
issues.description:
## Problem
Live credentials are in git history and readable from the Convex dashboard:
- ElevenLabs API key + Shopify Admin token (`.mcp.json` was tracked in git)
- Prod Convex `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` readable via `npx convex env list --prod`

The OpenAI key must be replaced anyway (BB-028), so rotate the whole set in one pass.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ElevenLabs key rotated; updated in Vercel, Convex, `.env.local`
- [ ] Shopify Admin token rotated (combine with BB-015 scope change)
- [ ] OpenAI + Anthropic keys rotated on prod Convex
- [ ] `.mcp.json` confirmed gitignored
- [ ] Old keys revoked and verified dead
- [ ] Consider history rewrite or accept and rotate

issues.title: Fix local env inconsistency (Convex dev vs prod)
issues.description:
## Problem
`.env.local` has `CONVEX_DEPLOYMENT=dev:helpful-elephant-638` while `NEXT_PUBLIC_CONVEX_URL` points at **prod** (`precise-raccoon-123`). The Convex CLI writes to dev while the app reads prod — an easy way to "fix" something invisibly, or to run a migration against the wrong deployment.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Documented in the README which combination is intended
- [ ] A guard or npm script that warns on mismatch

issues.title: Triage the ~40 open findings from the March 2026 UX audit
issues.description:
## Problem
`UX-AUDIT-REPORT.md` (411 lines, March 2026) holds ~40 severity-ranked findings that were never tracked to closure. Several were independently rediscovered in July:

| March finding | Rediscovered July |
|---|---|
| **H12a** Only 3 pricing tiers — missing production volume tiers | BB-005 |
| **C6** No shipping or lead time info anywhere in cart flow | BB-013 |
| **C5** No tier pricing nudge in cart | BB-003 |
| **M6** No "Request Quote" button in cart drawer | …which we then removed |

That last row is the point: M6 logged a gap, and five months later the opposite change shipped with nothing surfacing the contradiction.

## Method
Both March docs were *codebase walkthroughs* — inferred from source, never observed on a running site. That is why the expensive problems (410 checkouts, wrong prices charged) went unseen. Re-walk **against live staging**.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every March finding marked fixed / still-open / obsolete against staging
- [ ] Still-open findings become Linear issues linked to this one
- [ ] Obsolete findings struck with a reason
- [ ] Expect roughly a third done and a third stale

issues.title: Competitive study: 5 competitors, journey-based, evidence-backed
issues.description:
## Scope
Panel: **Calaso** (quote model, EU premium), **SKS/Pipeline Packaging** (US e-comm leader — note their site now says "SKS Bottle is now Pipeline Packaging", worth checking for consolidation), **Berlin Packaging** (largest US hybrid), **The Cary Company** (mid-market hybrid), **Baralan** (closest to Nemat's premium fragrance niche).

## Structure
Unit of analysis is **persona × journey step × site**, not page × site. Reuse the four existing personas so March scores stay comparable. Every row carries three columns: **legacy bestbottles.com / staging / best-in-class** — the legacy column is what surfaced the pricing regression and most audits omit it.

Store as machine-readable records in `data/competitive/` so quarterly re-runs can be diffed, with docs generated from them:
```
findings.jsonl      id, source, persona, journey, severity, status, owner, evidence[]
panel.json          sites + per-journey URLs
observations.jsonl  one row per (site × journey-step)
evidence/<site>/    screenshots + scraped markdown
```

## 12 fixed dimensions
Price visibility · tiers shown and where · cart model · MOQ/pack rounding · free-shipping threshold · published weights/dimensions · country of origin · stock visibility · fitment cross-sell · sample flow · account gating · lead times.

## Every finding ends in an owner tag
`code` / `content` / `abbas` — findings without an owner are how H12a stayed open five months.

## Already established (do not re-verify)
The pricing-display dimension is settled: legacy Best Bottles, SKS, and Calaso all surface the full ladder; the new site is the only one that doesn't.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Register populated for all 5 competitors + legacy + staging
- [ ] Matrix rendered with the three-way column
- [ ] Findings triaged into Linear with owner tags
- [ ] Re-runnable and diffable

issues.title: DECISION: which buyer persona are we optimizing for
issues.description:
## Context
The March analysis weights four personas equally: Decisive Buyer, Explorer, Overwhelmed Newcomer, Bulk/B2B Buyer. Jordan indicates it is **mostly B2B bulk, averaging 100–1,000 units per order**, with larger orders above that.

If that holds, two of the four personas are probably not who we are building for, which would let us drop a meaningful chunk of the March backlog rather than work it.

## Why it matters
At 100–1,000 units the B2B buyer cares, in order: correct price at their quantity, freight certainty, case/MOQ clarity, fast reorder. Discovery polish — where the rebuild is genuinely strong — matters less to them than any of those.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Primary and secondary personas confirmed
- [ ] March backlog re-scored against them; out-of-scope items closed as won't-do
- [ ] BB-044 dimensions weighted accordingly

issues.title: Restore legacy parity: tier ladder + quantity calculator on listing pages
issues.description:
## Problem
Legacy bestbottles.com puts the **full five-tier ladder and a live quantity calculator inline on the category page** — no click required, ~180 products per page:
```
GBV1DrmBlackCapSht
Pack Of : 1 pcs - $0.39/pc  12 pcs - $4.45($0.37/pc)  144 pcs - $50.54($0.35/pc)
          576 pcs - $190.94($0.33/pc)  2880 pcs - $876.10($0.30/pc)
Qty: [__]  Add to  →  Total Quantity: __   Price: __
```

The new catalog shows a "From $X" price and requires a PDP visit to see any tier at all.

## Trade-off worth being explicit about
The rebuild is far better at discovery — filters, sort, search, Grace, fitment — which legacy has **none** of (Filter count 0, Sort count 0). This is not "go back to the old site." It is: keep the discovery gains, restore the commercial density that a repeat B2B buyer relies on.

Depends on BB-005 (PDP ladder) landing first, and on BB-045 confirming the B2B buyer is primary.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Catalog cards show the tier ladder, or a compact "from $X at 144+" summary
- [ ] Quantity entry + add-to-cart from the listing for repeat buyers
- [ ] Does not degrade catalog performance (356 groups)
- [ ] Mobile layout verified

issues.title: Set up a launch smoke-test suite runnable against any environment
issues.description:
## Context
Several audit scripts already exist and each caught a real defect:
```
scripts/audit_launch_readiness.mjs          checkout/price/image coverage
scripts/audit_group_checkout_integrity.mjs  group→SKU FK integrity
scripts/audit_checkout_smoke.mjs            live checkout across families/tiers
scripts/audit_price_parity.mjs              Convex vs Shopify price parity
scripts/audit_shopify_sellability.mjs       full sellability sweep
scripts/audit_shipping_readiness.mjs        weights + carrier readiness
scripts/audit_typical_order_economics.mjs   100–1,000 unit order economics
```

## Task
One command that runs all of them against a chosen environment and fails loudly on regression, so launch readiness is a check rather than a memory.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `npm run audit:launch` runs the full set
- [ ] Non-zero exit on any launch-blocking regression
- [ ] Runs against staging and production by env var
- [ ] Documented in the README
